examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Definite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
examples.worked_solution:
Let $u=1-2x.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = -2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad -\dfrac 1 2 \,\textrm d u = \textrm d x.
$$

We also note that $x = \dfrac 1 2 (1-u).$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $0$ | $1/2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $1$ | $0$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}x(1-2x)^{5}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{0}\frac{1}{2}\cdot (1-u)\cdot {u}^{5}\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{0}(1-u)\cdot {u}^{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{0}({u}^{5}-{u}^{6})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{(\frac{1}{6}{u}^{6}-\frac{1}{7}{u}^{7})|}_{1}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}([0-0]-[\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{7}]) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(-\frac{1}{42}) \\  & =\frac{1}{168}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Let $u=x-2.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=u+2.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt{x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\int (u+2)\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int {u}^{3/2}+2{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}+\frac{4}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\sqrt{(x-2)^{5}}+\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{(x-2)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$
